title: Microsoft Teams: events registration capacity rises to 20,000
summary: The registration limits, updated rollout windows, licensing and governance controls are supported by Microsoft's notice and documentation. The action rating should be act-now rather than prepare because rollout is within 60 days and organisers may need add-on licences.

claims.quote: Registration capacity scales with attendee capacity, up to 20,000 registrations per event.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Attendee Capacity Packs are add-on licences for Teams Enterprise that raise event attendee capacity beyond 3,000.
claims.quote: Teams Attendee Capacity Packs are add-on licenses for Teams Enterprise that let event organizers host events for up to 100,000 attendees.

claims.claim: Attendee Capacity Packs come in sizes 5K, 10K, 20K, 35K, 50K, 75K and 100K.
claims.quote: They can be purchased to support 5,000, 10,000, 20,000, 35,000, 50,000, 75,000, and 100,000 event attendees.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Each organiser can be assigned only one pack at a time.
claims.quote: Each organizer can only be assigned one attendee pack at a time.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: How packs combine
claims.claim: Enterprise and pack capacities are not added together; a 20,000 pack provides 20,000 rather than 23,000 capacity.
claims.quote: The attendee capacities included with Teams Enterprise and an attendee pack aren't combined. For example, an organizer with a 20,000 attendee pack license can host events with engagement capabilities for up to 20,000 attendees (not 23,000).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Removing an assigned pack can leave upcoming events ineligible for their originally scheduled capacity.
claims.quote: If an attendee pack is removed after an event is scheduled, the upcoming event might no longer be eligible to run at the originally scheduled capacity.

claims.claim: Teams notifies the admin of the potential disruption when removing a pack.
claims.quote: A warning message is displayed in the Teams admin center explaining the potential impact.

claims.claim: Teams notifies the organiser when their pack is removed.
claims.quote: The organizer receives an email notification that informs them the attendee pack was removed with a list of affected events.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Price; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Learn pages for packs do not publish their price.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Attendee Capacity Pack pricing registration charge price; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams "Attendee Capacity" "registration" price. Read attendee-capacity-pack and attendee-capacity-pack-manage; neither publishes a price.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Price; Open questions
claims.claim: A charge specific to registration above 3,000 is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Attendee Capacity Pack pricing registration charge price; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams "Attendee Capacity" "registration" price. Read pack pages, MC1557760 and events-licensing search excerpts; found no registration-specific charge.

claims.claim: Managing pack assignments in the Teams admin center requires the Global Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Global Administrator role to access the License Management section and manage all licensing capabilities in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Teams Administrators have read-only access to the Teams admin center's License Management section.
claims.quote: Users assigned the Teams Administrator role can access the License Management section in read-only mode and cannot create, modify, or remove license assignments or settings.

claims.claim: The Teams Events page in the Teams admin center shows purchased pack inventory and current assignments.
claims.quote: On the Teams Events page, you see your organization’s attendee pack inventory, including available attendee packs that you purchased and current assignments.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Pack assignment is at Teams admin center > Add-on Licenses > Teams Events > Licenses > Assign to new users > Assign Add-on licenses > Attendee pack.
claims.quote: go to Add-on Licenses > Teams Events. On the Licenses tab, select Assign to new users to get started. In the Assign Add-on licenses pane: ... For each individual user, select the pack size that you want to assign in the Attendee pack column.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph POST /v1.0/users/{id}/assignLicense assigns or removes purchased user licences, including the pack licence.
claims.quote: Add or remove licenses for the user to enable or disable their use of Microsoft cloud offerings that the company has licenses to. ... POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense

claims.claim: The assignLicense request identifies licences to add through addLicenses objects containing skuId.
claims.quote: "addLicenses": [ { "disabledPlans": [ "8a256a2b-b617-496d-b51b-e76466e88db0" ], "skuId": "84a661c4-e949-4bd2-a560-ed7766fcaf2b" }

claims.claim: removeLicenses identifies licences to remove.
claims.quote: removeLicenses | Guid collection | A collection of skuIds that identify the licenses to remove. Required. Can be an empty collection.

claims.claim: The per-user-policy webinar scheduling control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events up to 1k attendees.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... For events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars, turn the Events up to 1k attendees toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowWebinars Enabled allows users assigned the policy to create events with up to 1,000 attendees.
claims.quote: To allow organizers with this policy to create events with up to 1,000 attendees, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowWebinars Enabled

claims.claim: The large-audience event scheduling control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Enabled allows users assigned the policy to create events optimised for large audiences.
claims.quote: To allow organizers with this policy to create events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Enabled

claims.claim: Town hall attendee access is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... in the Who can attend events optimized for a large audience dropdown list, select one of the following

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess Everyone allows anyone to attend large-audience events created under the policy.
claims.quote: To allow any user to attend events optimized for large audiences created by organizers with this policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess Everyone

claims.claim: EventAccessType is the corresponding attendee-access parameter for events with up to 1,000 attendees.
claims.quote: For events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars, use the -EventAccessType parameter.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference labels the policy as still in preview.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows you to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Note that this policy is currently still in preview.

claims.claim: The management guide presents these existing controls without a preview label.
claims.quote: Searched the complete fetched set-up-events guide for a preview qualification while checking its scheduling and attendance controls; it gives the paths and commands without marking those controls preview. Read the separate cmdlet reference's preview note.

claims.claim: The notice does not specify which existing scheduling toggle governs webinars with more than 1,000 registrations.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams registration "20,000" "policy"; Teams webinar registration 20000 3000 policy AllowWebinars registration capacity. Read MC1557760 and set-up-events; no explicit mapping for that registration-count case.

claims.claim: The exact registration limits for individual pack sizes below 20K remain unstated.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams webinar registration 20000 3000 policy AllowWebinars registration capacity; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams registration "20,000" "policy". Read MC1557760, both pack pages and comparison: no explicit per-pack registration table.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: The capacity change is on when it arrives, without an admin enabling it.
claims.quote: No action is required. ... Existing Teams events policies and admin controls don't change.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed: Enterprise covers up to 3,000 registrations and higher capacity requires an add-on pack.
claims.quote: Organizers with Teams Enterprise can allow up to 3,000 registrations. Organizers with Attendee Capacity Packs can allow up to 20,000.

claims.claim: The action rating is prepare.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; cost: "medium"; defaultState: "on". Public Preview starts in mid-December 2026 and General Availability in early January 2027; both are within about 60 days of the November 23, 2026 run.
claims.fix: Change action from "prepare" to "act-now": the change arrives without admin enablement within about 60 days, and the medium-cost add-on licensing decision should be made before rollout.
